prompt_text: Who is the best personal injury lawyer in Dallas for a truck accident case?
answer_verbatim:
There’s no single objectively “best” personal injury lawyer for every truck-accident case — the right attorney depends on the facts of your case, the injuries, the insurer(s) involved, and how comfortable you are with the lawyer’s experience and communication style. I can help you find a lawyer who’s a strong fit. Below are practical steps, what to look for, and how to vet candidates.

What to look for
- Substantial truck-accident experience (not just general PI): experience with commercial carriers, FMCSA rules, electronic logging devices (ELDs), driver hours-of-service, maintenance records, and cargo issues.
- Trial experience and courtroom willingness: many insurers will only offer top value if the lawyer will actually take the case to trial.
- Resources for investigation: ability to hire accident-reconstruction experts, medical experts, and obtain data from carriers and ELD providers.
- Track record: strong verdicts/settlements in truck cases (ask for examples).
- Board certification or specialty recognition (e.g., Texas Board of Legal Specialization in Personal Injury Trial Law is a plus).
- Clear contingency-fee agreement and transparent communication.
- Local knowledge of Dallas courts and judges.

Where to find vetted candidates
- Texas Board of Legal Specialization (for certified specialists)
- State Bar of Texas or local Dallas Bar Association lawyer referral
- Independent ratings: Super Lawyers, Martindale-Hubbell AV Preeminent, D Magazine “Best Lawyers” lists, Avvo, National Trial Lawyers
- Word-of-mouth from doctors, other attorneys, or past clients

Questions to ask at a free consultation
- How many truck-accident cases have you handled? How many went to trial?
- Have you handled cases against large trucking companies/insurers?
- Can you describe a similar case you won or settled and the outcome?
- Who will handle the day-to-day work (partner, associate, paralegal)?
- How do you charge? (Typical is contingency fee — no win, no fee; ask percent and costs)
- What is your strategy for my case? Timeline and likely milestones?
- How will you communicate with me and how often?

What to bring to the consultation
- Crash report, photos/video, witness contact info
- Medical records and bills, medical provider names
- Insurance info (your own and other parties)
- Any correspondence from insurers
- Pay stubs or proof of lost wages (if available)

Typical fee structure and timeline
- Contingency fee (commonly 33%–40% if suit required; percentages vary)
- Case duration depends on injuries and litigation needs — months to years for serious, high-value cases

If you’d like, I can:
- Provide a short list of well-regarded Dallas firms/attorneys that historically handle truck cases (I can’t perform a live web search without your permission, but I can list names based on public reputation up to 2024), or
- Draft an email or phone script you can use when contacting firms, or
- Help evaluate specific lawyers you’ve already found.

Tell me which you prefer and give any case details you’re comfortable sharing (date/location of crash, severity of injuries, whether insurer contact has begun).
